jobs.title: Principal Systems Engineer
jobs.description:
**ABOUT ROCKET LAB**

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity's reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

**SPACE SYSTEMS**

Rocket Lab's Space Systems division builds complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space including solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, and radios.

The Space Systems division has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. We have built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it's a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help get to space — our Space Systems division is empowering the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

**PRINCIPAL SYSTEMS ENGINEER**

Rocket Lab Optical Systems solves mission-critical space domain and Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance challenges for Department of Defense and Intelligence Community customers. Our vision is to revolutionize the space-based payload market with innovative and novel designs for space, terrestrial, and airborne environments. Building on more than 20 years of electro-optical and infrared systems innovation from Geost, Rocket Lab Optical Systems delivers solutions to the warfighter for responsive, scalable sensing solutions across all orbital domains.

As a Principal Systems Engineer for Rocket Lab Optical Systems in Tucson, AZ, you will be involved throughout the entire lifecycle of advanced space payloads in support of Tranche 3 of the U.S. Space Development Agency's Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture.

**WHAT YOU'LL GET TO DO:**

* Support the development of system architecture for space-based optical instruments, subsystems, and payloads on airborne and space platforms, with emphasis on electrical architecture and controls integration
* Define, decompose, and manage system requirements with focus on electrical behavior, control functions, subsystem interactions, and overall system performance
* Develop and maintain technical documentation including architecture descriptions, interface control documents, electrical interface definitions, concepts of operations, state and mode descriptions, test plans, and verification artifacts
* Support development of electrical and functional architectures, including command and telemetry flow, power distribution, control logic, signal paths, timing, synchronization, and subsystem interaction
* Collaborate with hardware, software, firmware, and test teams to ensure the electrical architecture and controls implementation align with system requirements and mission intent
* Support the development, integration, and testing of space payloads to be integrated on spacecraft platforms
* Support hardware and software development teams with system-level test planning, debugging, integration, and execution of verification procedures; analyze data and recommend design refinements
* Participate in hardware and software verification and validation activities related to system behavior, electrical performance, controls implementation, and interface compliance
* Support architecture trades involving sensors, motor control, embedded electronics, power systems, command and data handling, and subsystem interfaces
* Participate in technical interchange meetings and project discussions with internal teams, customers, and external partners as needed
* Identify, assess, and help mitigate technical risks related to electrical architecture, controls implementation, and subsystem integration
* Support travel or off-site work as needed
* Perform other duties as assigned

**QUALIFICATIONS YOU'LL BRING AS PRINCIPAL SYSTEMS ENGINEER:**

* Bachelor's degree in electrical, systems, or aerospace engineering; or other technical discipline
* 12+ years of engineering experience, including 3+ years supporting development programs and 2+ years in technical leadership, CAM, IPTL, or equivalent role
* Demonstrated systems engineering experience with emphasis on electrical architecture, subsystem integration, and controls focused development
* Strong electrical engineering background supporting complex aerospace, payload, avionics, or instrument systems
* Experience developing system requirements, interface definitions, and verification approaches for complex systems
* Strong background in electrical interfaces, control functions, avionics integration, or subsystem architecture
* Experience with requirements management and modeling tools such as JAMA, DOORS, Cameo, or similar tools
* Experience working across hardware, software, and firmware development throughout the lifecycle
* Familiarity with command and telemetry interfaces, power architectures, signal interfaces, timing, synchronization, and control logic
* Experience supporting integration and test, including troubleshooting electrical or controls-related issues at the subsystem or system level
* Strong ability to read, interpret, and develop electrical, interface, and system technical documentation
* Familiarity with aerospace development standards, environmental testing, and mission assurance practices

**THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:**

* Current SSBI clearance
* EO/IR payload integration experience
* Experience with spacecraft bus interfaces, payload electrical integration, avionics architecture, or embedded electronics
* Experience with pointing, stabilization, gimbals, motion control, focus/control electronics, or other closed-loop control applications
* Experience defining or troubleshooting elec

jobs.title: Embedded Systems Engineer
jobs.description:
**Embedded Systems Engineer**  
Bright Silicon Technologies | Pleasanton, CA | Full time

**About the Role**
==================

Bright Silicon Technologies (BST) is developing precision optical systems around our Lightfield Directing Array (LDA), a solid-state beam-steering technology. Our projects include OCTANE, a free-space laser communications terminal that brings together optics, electronics, and controls to connect moving platforms. Reliable embedded software makes that hardware work as a system.  
  
We’re looking for an Embedded Systems Engineer to develop the low-level and system software that connects these components together. This is a broad, hands-on engineering role spanning firmware, embedded Linux, device interfaces, hardware bring-up, system integration, and test. Because we are a small engineering team, the work can vary from writing real-time firmware and device drivers to performing hardware bring-up and characterization in the lab. You’ll work closely with electrical, controls, communications, photonics, and software engineers to move systems from early prototypes to dependable integrated hardware. We’re looking for someone who is comfortable working across these boundaries, learning unfamiliar technologies when needed, and taking ownership of problems that do not always fit neatly within one engineering discipline.

**What you’ll do**
==================

* Develop and debug C and C++ firmware and embedded software for device control, data acquisition, and communications. Carry your work from hardware bring-up through integration and validation.
* Work with electrical engineers to bring up new hardware and diagnose problems across electronics, firmware, and software. Use measurements and targeted experiments to understand timing, performance, and reliability.
* Use oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, debuggers, protocol analyzers, and other laboratory instrumentation to measure system behavior and investigate timing, signal, performance, and reliability problems.
* Partner with controls, integration, communications, and photonics engineers to deploy algorithms and connect subsystems on target hardware. Provide dependable device access, timing, telemetry, and diagnostic interfaces.
* Lead design and code reviews, share knowledge, and support other engineers through implementation and debugging. Document decisions so the team can build on each other’s work.
* Strengthen automated builds, hardware testing, and release practices. Make software configurations reproducible and failures easier to diagnose as systems move from the lab toward deployment.

**What we’re looking for**
==========================

* Strong C and C++ development skills and experience delivering embedded software on physical hardware. You’ve taken responsibility for a subsystem through bring-up, integration, and validation.
* Experience with bare-metal firmware, an RTOS, or embedded Linux. You understand how concurrency, interrupts, memory, and execution timing affect system behavior and can investigate performance problems.
* Hands-on hardware and software debugging experience. You can read schematics, work with device documentation, and use debuggers, oscilloscopes, or logic analyzers to trace a problem to its cause.
* Experience implementing device interfaces and communications, such as SPI, I2C, UART, or Ethernet. You can reason about latency, throughput, synchronization, and failure handling across connected components.
* A degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* U.S. citizenship - Position works on government projects requiring US Citizenship.

**Nice to have**
================

* Experience working with processor–FPGA systems or developing software interfaces to FPGA-based hardware.
* Familiarity with FPGA RTL development for timing, control, data acquisition, or digital interfaces.
* Experience with precision instruments, robotics, lidar, optical systems, or communications hardware.
* Familiar with Python or other scripting languages for test automation and lab tools; familiarity with MATLAB-based algorithm development and the work needed to deploy algorithms on embedded targets.
* Hardware-in-the-loop testing, field diagnostics, or maintaining shared embedded components across multiple products.
* Experience leading engineers deliver coordinated technical work through planning, interface definition, reviews, or mentoring.

Don't meet every single requirement? Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single qualification. At BST we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you're excited about this role but your past experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

**Why BST**
===========

* Help shape the embedded software behind a new optical technology, with work spanning hardware bring-up, system integration, and deployment.
* Lead through hands-on engineering and collaboration with experienced colleagues in software, electronics, controls, precision mechanisms, and optics.
* Take meaningful technical ownership in an engineer-led company with competitive compensation, equity, and a sustainable approach to work.

**Company Overview**
====================

At Bright, we build precision optical systems to guide data for a new era of communication. Our team combines precision engineering, optical design, and product development to commercialize the Lightfield Directing Array. Applications include laser communications, optical switching for data centers, lidar, and additive manufacturing.  
Founded in 2020, Bright Silicon Technologies is building an enduring technology manufacturing company. You’ll contribute to the development, launch, and scaling of advanced optical products.

jobs.description:
**About the Role**
==================

Bright Silicon Technologies (BST) develops precision optical systems built around our Lightfield Directing Array (LDA), a MEMS micromirror array for fast, precise control of light. Custom electronics drive and sense the motion of these devices, supporting applications in optical communications, tracking, and light control. Characterizing and integrating these electronics is central to advancing the LDA from research into reliable products.  
We’re looking for an electrical engineer to own the specification, qualification, and integration of custom silicon for our LDA technology. You’ll develop test boards, instrumentation, and automated test systems to characterize mixed-signal ASICs, evaluate their reliability, and integrate them with MEMS hardware. Working with our mechanical, software, production, and product teams, you’ll turn laboratory measurements and system requirements into validated hardware and specifications for the next generation of LDA devices.

**What you’ll do**
==================

* Lead the development of electronics and PCBAs for acceptance testing, performance qualification, and long-term reliability testing of custom ASICs for LDA applications.
* Develop environmental and reliability test plans and test apparatus, create schematics and PCB layouts, source components and board fabrication, validate hardware, and execute and scale test programs for silicon received from the foundry.
* Define requirements for custom ICs in next-generation LDA systems, including digital, analog, and high-voltage designs that improve performance, power consumption, size, cost, and supply chain resilience.
* Source components and services and manage relationships with external customers and vendors.
* Prepare clear technical documentation for internal use and external release.

**What we’re looking for**

* A bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* At least three years of relevant work experience.
* Experience in full-stack PCB design, including detailed specifications, design, hardware bring-up, and integration.
* Experience with ECAD tools such as Altium, Allegro/OrCAD, Eagle, KiCad, or equivalent.
* Experience using electronic test equipment and troubleshooting hardware issues.
* Experience with a numerical or scripting language such as Python, MATLAB, or equivalent.

* A master’s or doctoral degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field.

Colossus is bringing the computer revolution to space. Our goal is to take the last 30+ years of development in terrestrial computing to orbit. Colossus technology enables satellites to operate autonomously, facilitating instant Earth intelligence, satellite servicing, new modes of scientific exploration, and more. We touch every layer of the engineering design, from silicon to software to build solutions for the harsh environment of space.

**About This Role**

**Location:** Santa Clara, CA

**Work Location**: In-Person | Full-time | Relocation not offered

HYFIX Spatial Intelligence is building the next generation of autonomous drones and

robotic lawnmowers for dynamic, unstructured outdoor environments. Our systems

enable precision landscaping, spatial mapping, and property maintenance that scales

seamlessly, built on top of our proprietary RTK stack. We are developing fully

autonomous systems with no humans in the loop and are looking for a Robotics

Bright Silicon Technologies (BST) is developing precision optical systems around our Lightfield Directing Array (LDA), a solid-state beam-steering technology.
